solutions.check: 28 entries verified against the grid (lengths, crossings, linked-clue mapping)

clue.text: 'Toilet' article about Reagan shortened

indicators.note: to be about something is to surround it, so one piece wraps round another

parts.note: the definite article
Ronald Reagan's first name cut to its familiar short form

explanation.surface: A satirical piece about Reagan has been trimmed and labelled with a rude word.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shortened' looks like it applies to the article, but it turns Ronald into Ron; the quotation marks flag 'Toilet' as slang to be defined.
explanation.definitionFit: Throne is jokey colloquial slang for a lavatory, the seat one sits upon in the bathroom.

clue.text: Provocative, coarse inner city ad (Time Out)

indicators.note: coarse, as in rough and unrefined, signals the letters that follow are knocked into a new shape
Time Out, in brackets, tells us the time letter is left out of the mix

explanation.surface: A crude inner-city advert gets a write-up in the listings magazine Time Out.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the letters of INNER CITY AD, remove a T ('Time Out'), and rearrange the rest ('coarse'). Time Out is a London listings magazine, which hides the instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: Something incendiary is inflammatory, deliberately stirring up anger or conflict, as a provocative remark does.

clue.text: Prone to outbursts against "laconic" screwing

parts.note: V for versus, meaning against

indicators.note: screwing twists things round, so the letters are twisted into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone hot-tempered rails against terse speech, with a cheeky Private Eye double meaning on screwing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Screwing' reads as innuendo but only signals rearranging the letters of 'laconic'.
explanation.definitionFit: A volcanic temper erupts suddenly and violently, so a person described this way is liable to explosive fits of rage.

clue.text: George Eliot? Pound? New answer: Cyclops

parts.note: a pound is an enclosure for animals, as is a pen
N is the abbreviation for new
A is the abbreviation for answer
the setter refers to themselves, so Cyclops is me

explanation.surface: A list of literary names: Eliot, the poet Ezra Pound, and the setter himself.
explanation.walkthrough: Pound looks like the poet next to another writer, but it is an enclosure; Cyclops is the setter's own pseudonym, so it is both ME and an example of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: George Eliot was the pseudonym used by novelist Mary Ann Evans, a classic example of an author's assumed name; the question mark signals the example.

clue.text: A tiresome thing to read, Starmer's main set of principles

indicators.note: the main part is the head, so only the opening letter is kept

parts.note: the first letter of the name
a creed is a set of beliefs or principles

explanation.surface: Keir Starmer's lengthy statement of values is a dull document to plough through.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Starmer's main set of principles' reads as one phrase, but 'main' only takes the first letter of Starmer.
explanation.definitionFit: A screed is a long, tedious piece of writing, typically a rant or harangue that wearies the reader.

clue.text: Eddy goes topless — sexual desire?

indicators.note: losing one's top means losing the head, so the opening letter is dropped

parts.note: an eddy or surge is a swirling rush of water

explanation.surface: A man called Eddy strips off his shirt, which hints at lust.
explanation.walkthrough: Eddy reads as a man's name but is a swirl of water; removing the first letter of SURGE leaves the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An urge is a strong impulse or craving; the question mark admits that sexual longing is only one kind of such impulse.

clue.text: For someone who likes to lie about Corbyn's main row with right

parts.note: re is Latin-derived for about or concerning

indicators.note: the main part is the head, so only the opening letter is kept

parts.note: the first letter of the name
a row is a line
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A habitual liar spreads untruths about Jeremy Corbyn's big quarrel with the political right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lie' suggests telling untruths, but the person lies back; 'row' is a line, not a quarrel.
explanation.definitionFit: A recliner leans back or lounges at rest, being one who reposes horizontally rather than one who deceives.

clue.text: Shut up, accepted shag, US-style, showing a bit of leg

parts.note: sh is the call for silence
accepted into a group is in
bone is American slang for having sex

explanation.surface: A saucy scene: a silenced lover agrees to American-style sex while flashing some leg.
explanation.walkthrough: Shag is British slang for sex, and its American slang equivalent is bone.
explanation.definitionFit: The shinbone, or tibia, is the large front bone of the lower leg, so it is literally part of a limb.

clue.text: State right to sanction backing for criminal organisation?

parts.note: CA is the abbreviation for California
R is the abbreviation for right

indicators.note: going backwards runs the letters from end to start

parts.note: to sanction is to allow, to let

explanation.surface: A government's right to approve support for organised crime is questioned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Backing' looks like support for the organisation, but it turns the word for sanction round.
explanation.definitionFit: A cartel is a group of firms colluding to fix prices, and drug cartels are notorious crime syndicates, hence the question mark.

clue.text: (& 13ac.) Finally, Kate Middleton's about to tuck into very good Russian speciality

indicators.note: the rearranged letters are tucked in between the two letters for very good

parts.note: VG is the usual abbreviation for very good, as on a school report

indicators.note: about, as in all around, signals the letters are scattered and reformed
finally picks the last letter

parts.note: its last letter is E
the surname Middleton supplies its letters, the 's standing for 'is', a link

explanation.surface: Kate Middleton is finally about to tuck into a fine Russian delicacy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Finally' Kate gives E; with MIDDLETON, 'about' rearranges those ten letters, and they go 'to tuck into' VG. The 'Russian speciality' is the alleged interference in Western elections, not caviar.
explanation.definitionFit: Russia has been repeatedly accused of interfering in foreign elections, so tampering with ballots is presented sardonically as a national delicacy.

clue.text: Bit of fire shown by singer — what a pantomime!

parts.note: a cinder is a fragment of burnt fuel from a fire
Ella Fitzgerald, the jazz singer

explanation.surface: A singer shows a flash of fiery temper, and an onlooker sighs at the theatrical fuss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'What a pantomime!' sounds like exasperation at a fuss; pantomime is the British Christmas stage show for families, and this story is a favourite.
explanation.definitionFit: The rags-to-riches fairy tale is among the most frequently staged British Christmas family theatre shows, with ugly sisters and a glass slipper.

clue.text: Fibrous tissue not about to cramp butt

indicators.note: to cramp is to hem in tightly, so one piece is squeezed inside another
turning about faces the other way, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: taken as written
a butt is the end of something, as in a cigarette butt

explanation.surface: A sinew that will not give your backside a cramp.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cramp' suggests a muscle spasm, but it only signals one piece pressed inside another.
explanation.definitionFit: A tendon is the tough band of connective collagen that attaches muscle to bone, a classic example of such tissue.

clue.text: see 10ac.
MPs collectively raise the roof? On the contrary

parts.note: the opposite of raise, as the closing instruction demands
a roof over one's head is a home, so roof stands for a house

explanation.surface: Do MPs all together make a rowdy din? Quite the reverse.
explanation.walkthrough: To raise the roof is to make a racket; 'On the contrary' flips raise to its opposite, while roof stands for the whole building, as in a roof over your head.
explanation.definitionFit: The Commons, where elected Members of Parliament sit, is the lower chamber of the British legislature.

clue.text: Loan from a former Secretary of State cut by Donald at first

indicators.note: something cut by another is split open with it inserted in the gap

parts.note: taken as written
Cyrus Vance, US Secretary of State under President Carter

indicators.note: at first points to the beginning, so only the opening letter is kept

parts.note: the first letter of the name

explanation.surface: A loan from an ex-Secretary of State is slashed by Donald Trump.
explanation.walkthrough: Donald suggests Trump, but only his initial is used, splitting A from VANCE.
explanation.definitionFit: An advance is money paid or lent ahead of time, such as a payment against future wages or royalties.

clue.text: Ridiculed and kicked out of bed?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: exposed as false and made to look foolish
second meaning, whimsical: removed from one's bunk

explanation.walkthrough: The second meaning splits the word as DE- (removed from) plus BUNKED; the question mark flags the invented sense.
explanation.definitionFit: To debunk a claim is to expose it as hollow or sham, which holds it up to scorn and mockery.

clue.text: Ornate arch imprisons debtor

indicators.note: a prison holds someone inside it, so one piece is locked within another

parts.note: arch and fly both mean knowing or sly
a debtor is one who owes

explanation.surface: A decorated archway serves as a jail for a man who cannot pay, like an old debtors' prison.
explanation.walkthrough: Arch looks like the architectural curve, but it is the adjective meaning cunning, as is fly in British slang.
explanation.definitionFit: Flowery language or decoration is elaborate and full of embellishment, florid rather than plain.

clue.text: Perceived duration of Brexit and Coronavirus? I (and millions) feel pissed with it!

definitions.text: Perceived duration of Brexit and Coronavirus?

indicators.note: pissed is British slang for drunk, and drunk things lurch into disorder

parts.note: taken as written
M is the abbreviation for million
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Brexit and the pandemic seem to have lasted forever, and the setter and millions more are fed up.
explanation.walkthrough: In British slang pissed means drunk, not angry as in American usage; either way it signals the shuffle.
explanation.definitionFit: Both ordeals dragged on so long they seemed to occupy a whole existence, a jokey exaggeration of their length.

clue.text: Republican wants gene modification and city emptied — that's the style!

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for Republican

indicators.note: a modification alters the form, so the letters are changed round

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: emptying removes the contents, leaving only the outside letters

parts.note: only the first and last letters remain

explanation.surface: A Republican politician backs genetic engineering and clearing a city, calling it his preferred way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'That's the style!' sounds like approval, but it defines a named style of design.
explanation.definitionFit: Regency is the elegant early nineteenth-century British style of architecture, furniture and dress, named after the Prince Regent's rule.

clue.text: Suspended state of a singer-songwriter, giving away sod all and taking one in

indicators.note: giving away says a letter of her name is surrendered
taking, with in, says another letter is brought into the gap
in completes taking in: the new letter goes in where the old one was

parts.note: Beyoncé is the American singer-songwriter
sod all is slang for nothing, which is the letter O
one is A, as in a single thing

explanation.surface: A singer-songwriter in a state of limbo, giving away nothing and taking one in.
explanation.walkthrough: The singer is Beyoncé: 'giving away' sod all and 'taking' one 'in' swaps her O for an A, after the clue's opening A. 'Sod all' is British slang for nothing at all, and nothing is O.
explanation.definitionFit: Abeyance is a condition of temporary suspension or disuse, as when a plan or law is held in abeyance.

clue.text: Barely adequate food books dumped in river

indicators.note: something dumped in a place is put inside it

parts.note: the river Nile
B is book, so two of them make books

explanation.surface: Meagre rations and a pile of books thrown into a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Food' looks like a separate item in the list, but the whole opening phrase defines a light snack.
explanation.definitionFit: A nibble is a small bite or snack, a morsel hardly enough to satisfy anyone's hunger.

clue.text: Pursuing female, carry nuts a long way

indicators.note: pursuing means following behind, so this piece comes after the other

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for female

indicators.note: nuts means crazy, so the letters go wild into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A man chasing a woman carries nuts a great distance, perhaps as a gift.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Carry nuts' looks like transporting snacks, but nuts tells you to rearrange carry.
explanation.definitionFit: To be a far cry from something is to be very remote or different from it, an idiom for great distance.

clue.text: Which hosts dodgy union discussions

definitions.meaning: setter's reading: an organisation that counsels couples whose marriage, a union, is in trouble
surface reading: shady talks in a trade union, perhaps with crooked officials

explanation.surface: Something plays host to murky trade union negotiations.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is the name of a British charity that offers marriage and relationship counselling; union means a marriage, and dodgy means in difficulty.
explanation.definitionFit: The British charity offers counselling sessions to couples whose partnerships are struggling, hosting talks between troubled spouses.

clue.text: Crazy mom bent on a little amusement comes to a monumental ending

indicators.note: on places the second piece after the first
crazy letters are deranged, so mom bent is rearranged

parts.note: ent is a short form of entertainment, so a little of a word for amusement

explanation.surface: A mad mother, bent on a bit of fun, meets a grand and stony end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crazy' rearranges MOM BENT into ENTOMBM; 'a little amusement' is ENT, entertainment cut short, which goes 'on' the end. The definition plays on monument: a tomb is a monument, and burial is an ending.
explanation.definitionFit: Entombment is burial in a tomb, a final resting in a grave monument, hence a monumental conclusion to life.

clue.text: (& 26ac.) Some ponce on Lycra: "Never again!"

indicators.note: some means a portion, so the letters are a part of a longer stretch

parts.note: a run of letters spanning the three words

explanation.surface: An onlooker vows never again after seeing a vain man in tight cycling gear.
explanation.walkthrough: Ponce is British slang for a vain, showy man; the answer runs across his outfit.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying something happens once only means it will not be repeated, the same as vowing it will never happen a second time.

clue.text: see 25dn.
Member firmly has lead in this

definitions.text: Member firmly has lead in this

parts.words: Member firmly has lead in this
parts.note: surface reading: a smutty boast about a man's virility; setter's reading: a writing tool with graphite firmly fixed inside it

explanation.surface: A cheeky boast about male potency, in Private Eye's schoolboy style.
explanation.walkthrough: The idiom 'lead in your pencil' means sexual vigour, so Member hints at the body; read literally, the clue describes what the graphite is held in.
explanation.definitionFit: A writing implement holds a graphite core, traditionally called lead, set firmly inside its wooden casing.

clue.text: Temporary housing location — state politician: "It's bursting with energy!"

parts.note: CA is the abbreviation for California

indicators.note: bursting breaks something apart, so the letters are scattered and rearranged

parts.note: MP, a Member of Parliament
taken as written
E is the symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A state politician promotes a site for temporary homes as full of vigour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bursting with energy' reads as enthusiasm, but bursting rearranges the letters of 'it's' together with E.
explanation.definitionFit: A campsite is a place where tents or caravans are pitched, giving short-term shelter rather than permanent homes.
